summary: TPM ownership lock prevents provisioning on Dell Latitude 7440 after new provisioning image
description:
Issue summary: Several freshly imaged Dell Latitude 7440 notebooks fail during our onboarding script because the TPM is in a locked/owner-conflict state. The failure prevents machine identity provisioning (SSO device registration) and disk encryption enrollment. Impact: blocking day-0 setup for at least 6 new hires; slows inventory refresh for 12 staging units.

Observed behavior: After imaging with redwood-provision-2026.q1 (Ubuntu 22.04-based image), the provisioning agent exits with code 70 and shows 'tpm2_clear: failed to clear TPM: 0x000001c'. BitLocker/Drive encryption step fails and SSO device registration never completes.
steps_to_reproduce:
1) Boot Dell Latitude 7440 from PXE and run redwood-provision-2026.q1 image.
2) Let post-install scripts run (fw-updates, install packages, run onboarding-agent).
3) Observe onboarding-agent logs at /var/log/onboard.log or systemd unit redwood-onboard.service.
4) On failure, run tpm2_clear or tpm2_takeownership manually and observe error 'TPM RC: 0x1c (auth conflict / lockout)'.
logs:
Excerpt from /var/log/onboard.log: 
Mar 11 09:42:13 onboard[2145]: Running tpm2_clear to ensure fresh owner...
Mar 11 09:42:13 onboard[2145]: tpm2_clear: error: failed to run TPM2_Clear: rc 0x1c (auth conflict)
Mar 11 09:42:13 onboard[2145]: onboarding-agent: fatal: TPM not provisionable, aborting provisioning.
Kernel dmesg snippet: tpm_tis 00:0a: TPM is a TPM2.0 device, 0x1c owner conflict flag set.
investigation_notes:
Initial hypothesis: Provisioning script expects a software-clearable TPM. Multiple units report a firmware-level lock/owner state that rejects software clears.
What we tried:
- Manual tpm2_clear as root (reproduces error).
- Clearing TPM via OS (fails).
- Boot to BIOS and attempt TPM clear via menu (succeeds only when performed interactively with admin password).
- Cross-tested same image on Lenovo T14 and no failure observed.
- Checked fwupd metadata and found a recently applied Dell firmware (SEC-2026-02) that introduced 'Enhanced TCG profile' default on some Latitude 7440 serial ranges.
Findings: Certain fresh units ship with an OEM firmware flag that prevents software-initiated TPM ownership clear; BIOS requires explicit interactive clear or admin provisioning (or firmware update that toggles profile). This breaks our unattended provisioning flow.
comments: Support (Aisha): Reported new-hire laptop failures, collected 6 affected serials and forwarded to Eng.
Infra (Marco): Reproduced in staging. Confirmed tpm2_clear returns 0x1c on affected serials. Filed for firmware correlation.

Firmware (Lena Ortiz): Dell advisory found for firmware SEC-2026-02; some units now default to 'TPM profile: enhanced' which locks owner to OEM until user clear at BIOS. Dell recommends applying OEM tool or interactive BIOS clear.
Support (Aisha): Applied manual BIOS TPM clear for 2 units as workaround and re-ran provisioning — success. Not scalable for remote new hires.
Engineering (Marco): Drafted imaging patch to include a pre-provision check and a fallback user-flow that instructs IT to clear TPM in BIOS when automatic clear fails.
resolution:
Workaround implemented: (1) Add detection in provisioning pipeline to detect 0x1c owner conflict and mark device for manual BIOS clear or remote support intervention. (2) For staging and on-prem bulk provisioning, include interactive TPM clear step at imaging station.
Permanent fix / follow-ups: (A) Add fwupd/bios check to redwood-provision-2026.q2 to apply Dell firmware patch that allows automated clear where safe. (B) Create a playbook and automation ticket for IT ops to perform a remote BIOS TPM clear via Dell Command | Configure on affected serial ranges. (C) Inventory script to flag incoming Latitude 7440 units falling into impacted firmware serial ranges.
